gloss: forcibly; compulsorily; if pressed; if I must say

definitions.explanation: Doing something against one's will or nature, or making someone do something unwillingly.

definitions.gloss: if pressed; if I must say; dare I say
definitions.explanation: Used when offering an opinion reluctantly or when pressed to give an answer even though one doesn't have a strong opinion.

examples.japanese: {強|し}いて⟦{参加|さんか}する→参加：02498_sanka⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧。
examples.english: You don't need to force yourself to participate.

examples.japanese: ⟦{嫌|いや}がる→嫌がる：03041_iyagaru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{強|し}いて⟦{飲|の}ませる→飲む：00322_nomu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よくない→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: It's not right to force someone to drink when they don't want to.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{他人|たにん}→他人：01459_tanin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{強|し}いて⟦はいけない→いけない：02335_ikenai⟧。
examples.english: You shouldn't force your opinions on others.

examples.japanese: {強|し}いて⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧⟦なら→なら：09575_nara⟧、⟦こっち→こっち：02903_kocchi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ほう→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦かもしれない→かもしれない：00164_kamoshirenai⟧。
examples.english: If I had to choose, this one might be better.
If I had to say, I guess I like blue more than red.

examples.japanese: {強|し}いて⟦{挙|あ}げる→挙げる：27889_ageru⟧⟦なら→なら：09575_nara⟧、⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{足|た}りなかった→足りる：01209_tariru⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: If I had to point out something, the problem was that we didn't have enough time.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The て-form of the verb ⟦{強|し}いる→強いる：15604_shiiru⟧ (to force, to compel), now fixed as an adverb.

SENSE 1 - FORCIBLY:
Doing something, or making someone do something, against their inclination:
・{強|し}いて〜⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to do ~ by force, to force oneself to ~)
・{強|し}いて〜させる (to force someone to ~)
It is most often negated: {強|し}いて〜⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ (there is no need to force it), {強|し}いて⟦はいけない→いけない：02335_ikenai⟧ (you must not force it). A plain affirmative sounds stiff and literary.

SENSE 2 - IF PRESSED:
Followed by a conditional, this is one of the most useful hedges in spoken Japanese:
・{強|し}いて⟦{言|い}えば→言う：00515_iu⟧ (if I had to say)
・{強|し}いて⟦{挙|あ}げる→挙げる：27889_ageru⟧⟦なら→なら：09575_nara⟧ (if I had to name one)
・{強|し}いて⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧⟦なら→なら：09575_nara⟧ (if I had to choose)
The speaker is signalling that they have no strong preference and are answering only because they were asked, so the opinion that follows should not be weighed too heavily. Sentence-final ⟦かな→かな：10989_kana⟧ or ⟦かもしれない→かもしれない：00164_kamoshirenai⟧ often softens it further.

SIMILAR ADVERBS:
・⟦あえて→あえて：06074_aete⟧ - to do something deliberately despite the difficulty or the reasons not to; a positive choice, where {強|し}いて is closer to reluctance
・⟦{無理|むり}やり→無理やり：10526_muriyari⟧ - forcibly, by brute force; blunter and more physical than sense 1, and never used for the hedging sense
